options.text: the popular acceptance that a government's power is rightful
the size of the armed forces a government controls
the number of political parties allowed to contest elections
the length of time a government has been in office

questions.explanation: Legitimacy is a belief held by the governed, not a resource held by the government. Where that belief is strong, people obey because they think they ought to, and coercion becomes the exception.

distractorRationale.b: Military strength supplies power, and heavy reliance on it usually signals weak legitimacy
distractorRationale.c: The number of parties describes the party system, not the rightfulness of the government
distractorRationale.d: Long tenure may be the result of legitimacy, but a long-lasting dictatorship shows it is not the definition

questions.stem: Which of the following is the strongest source of legitimacy for a civilian government?

options.text: Control of the state broadcasting service
Victory in a free, fair and credible election
Ownership of the largest share of national wealth
The deployment of soldiers in every major city

questions.explanation: A credible election is the clearest expression of popular consent, and consent is what converts power into rightful authority. It also gives the losers a rule-governed route back, which is why electoral legitimacy stabilises a state.

distractorRationale.a: Controlling the media may shape opinion, but manufactured support is not freely given consent
distractorRationale.c: Wealth confers economic power, not the right to govern
distractorRationale.d: Widespread military deployment is a sign that voluntary obedience is missing

questions.stem: A government that has lost legitimacy is most likely to

options.text: rely increasingly on force to secure compliance
attract greater voluntary obedience to its laws

questions.explanation: When people no longer accept a government's right to rule, they obey only when watched, so the regime must substitute coercion for consent. A rising security budget alongside falling tax compliance is the classic symptom.

distractorRationale.a: Security spending typically rises, not falls, as legitimacy declines
distractorRationale.c: Tax compliance falls when citizens deny the government's right to demand payment
distractorRationale.d: Voluntary obedience is precisely what a loss of legitimacy destroys

questions.stem: The process by which an individual acquires political beliefs, attitudes and values is called political
questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the lifelong learning process that transmits political culture, working through the family, school, peer group, religious bodies, mass media and political parties.

distractorRationale.a: Political apathy is a lack of interest in politics, which may itself be one outcome of socialisation
distractorRationale.c: Political participation is the activity of taking part, not the process of acquiring beliefs
distractorRationale.d: Political obligation is the duty to obey the state, a separate concept

questions.stem: Citizens who are aware of national government but see themselves purely as recipients of its decisions rather than as participants exhibit what Almond and Verba called a
questions.explanation: In the subject culture the citizen knows the state exists and expects to be affected by it, but does not expect to influence it. Awareness without a sense of competence to act is the defining combination.

distractorRationale.a: In a parochial culture citizens are barely aware of the national government at all
distractorRationale.c: Participant citizens believe they can and should shape government decisions
distractorRationale.d: Almond and Verba used civic culture for a healthy blend of the three, not for this passive type

questions.stem: An action of government may be legal and yet lack legitimacy.
questions.explanation: True. Legality tests whether the correct procedure was followed; legitimacy tests whether the people accept the act as rightful. A properly enacted but deeply resented law is legal without being legitimate.

distractorRationale.b: This treats the two as identical, which would make popular resistance to lawful but unjust measures impossible to explain

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT normally regarded as an agent of political socialisation?
questions.explanation: Agents of socialisation are institutions that teach political values through sustained contact with the individual. Census figures are statistical data; they inform planning but do not shape a child's political outlook.

distractorRationale.a: The family is the earliest and often the most durable agent
distractorRationale.b: Schools transmit civic values through curriculum, prefect systems and school elections
distractorRationale.c: Media coverage shapes what citizens think politics is and how it works

questions.stem: A military regime that seized power unconstitutionally but restored order and built roads is said to enjoy
questions.explanation: Where a regime cannot point to the constitution or the ballot box, acceptance can still rest on results delivered. Such performance legitimacy is fragile, because it collapses the moment delivery falters.

distractorRationale.a: The regime broke the constitution to take power, so it cannot claim this basis
distractorRationale.b: No election was held, so there is no electoral mandate
distractorRationale.d: Traditional legitimacy rests on inherited custom, which a modern coup regime does not possess
